easy.def: A word that shows something belongs to me.
examples: This is my hat.
My dog is brown.
I love my mom.

more.def: A word a speaker or writer uses to show that something belongs to them or is connected to them.
examples: My grandmother lives in a small house by the sea.
I finished my project before the deadline.
My favorite subject is science.
I did it myself.
I made myself lunch.
I hurt myself.

more.def: A word a speaker uses for themselves, when they do something to themselves or without help.
examples: I built the birdhouse all by myself.
I looked at myself in the mirror before school.
I taught myself how to whistle.
A mysterious light was in the sky.
The mysterious box was locked.
The sound was mysterious.

more.def: Hard to understand or explain, and full of secrets.
examples: A mysterious light blinked in the woods.
The mysterious letter had no name on it.
A mysterious fog covered the lake.

easy.def: Something we do not understand or know yet.
examples: Who took the cookie? It is a mystery!
My book is a mystery.
Where the cat goes at night is a mystery.

more.def: Something that is hard to explain or that has not been solved.
examples: How the huge stones were moved is still a mystery.
The detective solved the mystery of the missing ring.
Deep space is still full of mystery.

easy.def: A person who seeks deep truths through prayer.
examples: The mystic prayed.
A mystic lived in the cave.
The mystic was wise.

more.def: A person who seeks to understand deep spiritual truths through prayer, quiet thinking or special experiences.
examples: The mystic lived alone in the mountains and spent his days in prayer.
In the story, a mystic told the king about a strange dream.
The mystic believed that all living things are connected.
The forest felt mystical.
A mystical light glowed.
She told a mystical tale.

more.def: Having a mysterious or spiritual feeling that is hard to explain.
examples: The misty forest at dawn had a quiet, mystical feeling.
A mystical light glowed over the lake in the old legend.
The wizard's mystical stone could not be explained by science.

easy.def: An old story that explains something.
examples: The myth tells about a god.
I read a myth.
A myth explains the sun.

more.def: An ancient story that tells about gods or heroes and explains how things came to be.
examples: We read a Greek myth about a hero.
A myth explains why the sun rises.
The old myth told of a giant.

easy.def: Something many people believe that is not true.
examples: It is a myth that bats are blind.
That is a myth.
The myth is false.

more.def: An idea that many people believe but that is not true.
examples: It is a myth that goldfish have a three-second memory.
The teacher cleared up a common myth.
The idea is just a myth.

easy.def: Made up in old stories, not real.
examples: A dragon is mythical.
The mythical bird flew.
A mythical land.

more.def: Existing only in myths or stories, and not real.
examples: A dragon is a mythical creature.
The mythical bird rose from the ashes.
The story tells of a mythical island.

easy.def: Old stories about gods and heroes.
examples: We read Greek mythology.
Mythology has dragons.
I like mythology.

more.def: A collection of old stories that people told about gods, heroes and monsters to explain the world.
examples: In Greek mythology, Zeus was the king of the gods.
We read stories from Norse mythology about thunder and giants.
Mythology tells how ancient people explained the sun and the seasons.
